historical_context: The 15cm sFH 18 was the standard German heavy divisional howitzer. Artillerie-Regiment 33's III. Abteilung (formerly independent s.Art.Abt. 647) provided 12 heavy howitzers for long-range fire support.

sFH 18 150mm.notes: Heavy howitzer for long-range bombardment. Very powerful HE round.

strengths: Very powerful HE round (43.5 kg shell)
Long range (13.325 km) for deep fires
Can destroy British gun positions and fortifications
weaknesses: Vulnerable to counter-battery fire when deployed
High fuel consumption for prime movers
tactical_notes.typical_deployment: Long-range bombardment of British defensive positions, fortifications, and assembly areas. Counter-battery fire against British 25-pdr batteries. Preparatory bombardment before major attacks. Support for siege operations (Tobruk). Usually held at regimental or divisional level for massed fire missions. Not as mobile as light 105mm batteries.

phase_6_data_source.organization: One battalion with 3 batteries of 4 guns each
phase_6_data_source.notes: Attached army-level heavy artillery battalion assigned to 15. Panzer-Division

historical_engagements.tobruk_siege: April-December 1941. Heavy howitzers used for bombardment of Tobruk fortress and counter-battery fire against Australian artillery.
historical_engagements.operation_battleaxe: June 15-17, 1941. Provided long-range fire support for defensive operations.
historical_engagements.effectiveness: Effective for siege operations and defensive fire. Less useful in mobile operations due to weight and deployment time.
